summary: Construct the character-admissible quotient of perverse sheaves on an abelian variety and its arithmetic and geometric convolution groups. Compute smooth ample hypersurface dimensions and Hodge data, use microlocal factorization and exterior-weight counting to classify connected derived monodromy, and obtain generic and Galois-uniform product monodromy for families. The period-map application records the precise dimension and trace-compatibility obligations that its proof still needs.

nodes.title: Geometric character space
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A over a characteristic-zero field k, a chosen algebraic closure k̄, and coefficient field F=Q̄_ℓ, put Π(A)=Hom_cont(π₁ᵉᵗ(A_k̄,0),F×). It is an abelian group under multiplication of characters. For a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety B⊂A_k̄, let T_B be the subgroup of characters trivial on the image of π₁ᵉᵗ(B,0). A torsion character has finite image; a torsion coset is τT_B with τ of finite order. On A^c use abelian subvarieties of A^c, including those coupling coordinates. This is a set with group structure; it is not asserted to be an algebraic F-torus.
hypotheses: char(k)=0; ℓ is a prime; all fundamental groups are geometric and based at the identity.
proofSteps: Import the geometric étale fundamental group, its finite-cover equivalence and the torsion/isogeny description for abelian varieties. Define the subgroup as a restriction kernel.
Use π₁(A×A′)=π₁(A)×π₁(A′) to identify product characters. Keep the algebraic Betti-character torus and continuous étale characters distinct.

nodes.title: Origin-normalized character sheaf
nodes.statement: For χ∈Π(A), construct the rank-one lisse F-sheaf Lχ on A_k̄ with monodromy χ. This is the unique descent with a chosen trivialization at 0 fixed by Galois. Its multiplicative structure a*Lχ≅Lχ⊠Lχ is normalized at (0,0) and coherent.

proofSteps: Apply the lisse sheaf/continuous representation equivalence. The invariant-character condition is precisely the compatibility needed to extend over the semidirect product.
Normalize the rank-one tensor isomorphism by the identity fibre, which forces associativity and the unit laws.

nodes.title: Derived sheaf convolution
nodes.statement: On Dᵇ_c(A,F), define K*L=Ra_*(K⊠L), where a is addition and ⊠ is the derived external tensor product. With the symmetry inherited from complexes, including Koszul signs, this is a rigid symmetric monoidal structure. Its unit is δ₀ and its dual is K∨=[−1]*D_AK. Evaluation and coevaluation satisfy both triangle identities.
hypotheses: A is proper over k of characteristic zero; coefficients are F; constructible adic boundedness receipts are imported.
proofSteps: Obtain associativity, unit and symmetry by proper base change, the projection formula and the group law. Use the coherent six-operation comparisons, rather than equality of chosen derived models.
Construct evaluation from duality and the antidiagonal, as in Weissauer’s rigidity proposition; verify both triangle identities before passing to a quotient.

nodes.title: Generic vanishing on abelian varieties
nodes.statement: For a perverse F-sheaf K on a complex abelian variety, there is a finite union of translates of proper character subtori outside which H^j(A,K⊗Lχ)=0 for j≠0. The translating characters can be chosen torsion when K is semisimple of geometric origin. The same existence statement for continuous étale characters follows by the comparison and coefficient interfaces. A finite family of perverse sheaves admits one common good character; arbitrary non-geometric sheaves do not acquire torsion exceptional translates by this theorem.
hypotheses: For the torsion-coset assertion impose geometric origin; use the integral-lattice essential image in analytic/étale comparison.
proofSteps: Use KW Theorem 1.1 for the cohomological vanishing and Lemma 11.2(c) for torsion translation in the geometric-origin case.
For finitely many composition factors take the union of their bad loci. Finite unions remain proper and admit continuous good characters; torsion good characters exist in the geometric-origin case.

sources.match: These two statements have different generality. The torsion conclusion is not part of the arbitrary-perverse version.

nodes.title: Negligible perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: For K perverse on A set χ(A,K)=Σ_j(−1)^j dim_F H^j(A_k̄,K_k̄). Let N be the full subcategory with χ(A,K)=0, and let D_N be the full subcategory of Dᵇ_c whose every perverse cohomology object lies in N. N is a Serre subcategory and D_N is a thick triangulated subcategory stable under convolution with arbitrary constructible complexes. For perverse K,L, pH^j(K*L)∈N when j≠0.
hypotheses: Geometric Euler characteristic; constructible field coefficients, finite-dimensional cohomology.
proofSteps: Prove nonnegativity by generic vanishing. Additivity in perverse short exact sequences then proves the Serre assertion.

Use finitely many perverse cohomology objects and a common generic character to prove the convolution ideal and nonzero-degree negligibility, following KW. Generic vanishing is established before the quotient and has no quotient prerequisite.

nodes.title: Character-admissible perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: For χ∈Π(A), define Pχ to be the full subcategory of perverse K on A for which H^j(A_k̄,Q⊗Lχ)=0 for every geometric perverse subquotient Q of K_k̄ and every j≠0. Set Nχ=Pχ∩N. Then Pχ is Serre and its essential image in P/N is equivalent to Pχ/Nχ. That image contains δ₀ and is closed under quotient convolution and rigid duals. A fixed χ suffices for a tensor category generated by any K belonging to Pχ.
hypotheses: χ need not be Galois-invariant for this definition or for a vector-space-valued geometric fibre functor.
proofSteps: Test the vanishing on the finitely many geometric composition factors; extension stability follows from the long cohomology sequence.
Use KW’s closure of the good subcategory under convolution and duality in the quotient, together with the Serre quotient comparison.

nodes.statement: For K∈Pχ let ⟨K⟩⊗ be the full Tannakian subcategory of Pχ/Nχ generated by Q(K) using tensor products, duals, finite sums and subquotients. For geometrically semisimple K over an algebraically closed field, G(K,χ) is reductive.

proofSteps: Apply abstract neutral reconstruction from MC.6, whose comodule special case is already in the pinned Tau Ceti library.

nodes.title: Arithmetic and geometric convolution categories
nodes.statement: Fix χ∈Π(A). Let C_ar be the full subcategory of Pχ/Nχ represented by geometrically semisimple perverse sheaves on A. Let C_geo be the full subcategory on A_k̄ consisting of direct summands of pullbacks of these objects. Both, with ωχ, are neutral Tannakian. For geometrically semisimple representatives K,L the quotient Hom is Hom_P(K,L) modulo maps factoring through N. C_geo is deliberately the category generated by arithmetic pullbacks, rather than the entire geometric perverse quotient.
hypotheses: k has characteristic zero. Geometric semisimplicity is imposed on pullbacks, not on the arithmetic representation at the origin.
proofSteps: Split each geometrically semisimple object into its negligible and nonnegligible geometric parts; Galois-stable isotypic projectors descend. This proves the Hom formula without asserting it for arbitrary objects.

Use the requested characteristic-zero proper-direct-image semisimplicity theorem for convolution. Semisimplicity then makes kernels, cokernels and geometric subobjects summands of arithmetic pullbacks.

nodes.title: Arithmetic–geometric exact sequence
nodes.statement: Let G_ar=Aut⊗(ωχ|C_ar), G_geo=Aut⊗(ωχ|C_geo), and Gal_k^alg be the Tannaka group of continuous finite-dimensional F-representations of Gal(k̄/k). There is an exact sequence of affine proalgebraic group schemes 1→G_geo→G_ar→Gal_k^alg→1: the first map is a closed immersion and the second faithfully flat, with scheme-theoretic kernel G_geo. Gal_k^alg is not identified with the profinite Galois group as a constant group scheme.
hypotheses: Categories and fibre functors are those of SC.2; coefficient field F has characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Apply EHS Theorem A.1 through the requested MC.6 interface. The origin-supported Galois embedding is full and stable under subquotients, giving faithful flatness.

Every geometric object embeds in a pullback. Objects becoming sums of geometric units are precisely origin-supported arithmetic objects modulo N. The maximal geometric unit subobject descends, by its canonical origin-supported projector. These verify kernel exactness, not merely normality on rational points.

nodes.title: Galois normalization of geometric monodromy
nodes.statement: Suppose χ is Galois-invariant and K on A is geometrically semisimple and belongs to Pχ. Using the origin-normalized descent Lχ, the continuous Galois action on ωχK normalizes the geometric convolution group G_K and hence (G_K°)^der. These groups are viewed in GL(ωχK) through the same fibre functor; changing χ conjugates the comparison.

proofSteps: The normalized descent defines tensor automorphisms of the arithmetic fibre functor for each Galois element.
Take the image of the normal geometric subgroup in GL(ωχK); identity component and derived subgroup are characteristic and are therefore preserved.

nodes.statement: For algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields k⊂K, A/k, and a constructible perverse F-sheaf Q defined over k, pullback identifies the tensor-generated convolution categories of Q and Q_K, their negligible quotients, and the represented convolution groups after choosing compatible fibre functors. This comparison is for the categories generated by the given object; it does not claim that every perverse sheaf over K descends to k.

nodes.title: Euler characteristics of a smooth ample divisor
nodes.statement: Let A be a complex abelian variety of dimension n≥2 and i:H↪A a smooth ample divisor, with L=O_A(H). Put d=[H]^n/n!=χ(A,L)>0 and N=[H]^n=n!d. Then χ(H,O_H)=(−1)^(n−1)d, e_top(H)=(−1)^(n−1)N, and χ(H,Ω_H^q)=(−1)^(n−1−q)d A(n,q) for 0≤q<n. Here A(n,q) counts permutations with q descents; for integral q outside [0,n−1] it is extended by zero. The n=0 convention of CA.2 is not overwritten.
hypotheses: H is smooth and ample; intersection degree is an integer; n≥2 ensures connectedness.
proofSteps: Use the imported abelian Riemann–Roch formula and vanishing to identify the positive integer d; the trivial tangent bundle and normal sequence give e_top(H) with the displayed sign.

Resolve Ω_H^q using the conormal exact sequence and the exterior powers of the trivial cotangent bundle of A. Apply line-bundle Riemann–Roch to the alternating Euler characteristics, and identify the resulting finite difference with the imported Eulerian formula.

sources.match: This is the hypersurface specialization. General Riemann–Roch and the Eulerian family already have owners and are not new definitions here.

nodes.title: Distinguished hypersurface representation
nodes.statement: For the smooth ample divisor H in SC.3, define K_H=i_*F[n−1] in the perverse category. Its image under a good ωχ is the distinguished representation V_H of G_H=G(K_H). It is irreducible, has dimension N=n!d>0, and identifies with H^(n−1)(H,Lχ|H). The shift is n−1, not n. The subgroup used in monodromy theorems is G_H*=(G_H°)^der.
hypotheses: Use a good character; H is geometrically connected and smooth.
proofSteps: The rank-one constant local system on the smooth connected support shifted by its dimension is a simple perverse sheaf; finite closed pushforward preserves it.
Its fibre dimension is its perverse Euler characteristic, which changes the topological sign to N>0. Identify degree-zero cohomology of the shift with middle unshifted cohomology.

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate row of a generic torsion twist
nodes.statement: Let A/k be an n-dimensional abelian variety over a finite extension k/Q_p, let H⊂A be smooth ample, and let χ be a finite-order geometric character for which H^j(H_k̄,Lχ)=0 when j≠n−1. After a finite extension k′ defining χ, its coefficients and normalized descent, V=H^(n−1)(H_k̄,Lχ) is Hodge–Tate. In the R06.2 convention HT(cyclotomic)=+1, weight −q occurs with multiplicity d A(n,q), for 0≤q<n. Thus the nonnegative label q used in LS is the negative of the native Hodge–Tate weight. No good-reduction hypothesis is needed.
hypotheses: p is the cohomological prime in this node; finite coefficients can be enlarged inside Q̄_p.
proofSteps: Realize the character-isotypic part of the cohomology of [m]⁻¹H using the finite étale A[m]-cover and its rational idempotent after coefficient extension. The idempotent is valid also when p divides m, since the coefficient field has characteristic zero.
Apply proper smooth comparison and its Hodge decomposition to each isotypic part. A torsion line-bundle twist has rational Chern character 1, so Riemann–Roch preserves the Ω-Euler characteristics.
Concentration of total cohomology and Hodge–de Rham degeneration isolate H^(n−1−q)(Ω^q⊗L), giving dA(n,q). Translate the source’s labels by h=−q.

nodes.title: Clean conormal cycle ring
nodes.statement: For a complex abelian variety A of dimension n set V=H⁰(A,Ω_A¹) and T*A=A×V. Let L(A) be the free abelian group on irreducible conic Lagrangian n-dimensional subvarieties Λ⊂A×V that dominate V (the clean components). The clean part discards nondominant components. Define degΛ by the generic Gauss-map degree and extend additively. For two generators restrict to a common open U⊂V on which both Gauss maps are finite flat, take their fibre product, push its cycle forward along addition A×A×U→A×U with generic degrees and multiplicities, and take the unique clean closure. Extend bilinearly to obtain ◦. This is a commutative ring with unit Λ_{0}; deg(Λ₁◦Λ₂)=degΛ₁ degΛ₂.
hypotheses: Cycle pushforward uses lengths and mapping degrees; an image support alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Construct the cycle group and clean projection from the imported algebraic-cycle operations. Shrink the finite flat Gauss open to make cycle intersections and addition pushforward well defined.
Show independence by restricting two choices to their common dense open and uniqueness of clean closure. Associativity comes from the triple fibre product; degrees multiply by finite-flat degree.

The map on Grothendieck groups is additive, respects convolution, and satisfies deg cc(K)=χ(A,K). For a smooth closed subvariety Z of dimension r with a rank-one constant local system, CC(i_*F[r]) is the conormal Λ_Z with multiplicity one. It respects translation, inversion duality and finite étale isogeny pushforward.

nodes.title: Microlocal tensor factorization
nodes.statement: Let K be a simple perverse object on a complex abelian variety, with positive Euler characteristic and translation stabilizer {0}. If Lie G(K) is not simple modulo its centre, there is an integer m>0 and nonzero effective clean cycles Λ₁,Λ₂, each of Gauss degree greater than 1, such that [m]_*cc(K)=Λ₁◦Λ₂. For a reduced irreducible conormal factor of the product, the addition correspondence supplies the rational support maps of K2 Lemma 5.2.2.
hypotheses: Use the regular-holonomic realization, where translation stabilizer and the tensor group agree with the perverse realization.
proofSteps: Use irreducibility on the identity component after killing translation stabilizers. Pull back to a central product cover of the connected reductive group and split its irreducible representation into two tensor factors.

Apply K2 Theorem 2.3.1 and the isogeny-clearing step to obtain integral effective cycles. The degree bounds reflect the nontrivial semisimple factors. Obtain the rational support maps from the reduced component as in Lemma 5.2.2.

nodes.title: Minuscule hypersurface representation
nodes.statement: Let H⊂A be smooth ample with no nonzero translation stabilizer. The restriction of V_H to G_H° is irreducible minuscule. Its characteristic cycle is the single reduced irreducible clean conormal Λ_H and is invariant under no nontrivial translation. This assertion applies for n≥2.
hypotheses: The dimension is N>0; use the faithful represented group, not a guessed simply connected covering group.
proofSteps: Compute the smooth characteristic cycle with shift [n−1] and use the index to show it is clean.

Apply K1 Corollary 1.10 to the irreducible conormal. Its Gauss monodromy is transitive, producing one Weyl orbit of weights; the trivial translation stabilizer removes disconnected-component ambiguity.

nodes.title: Simplicity modulo the centre
nodes.statement: If n>2 and H is a smooth ample divisor on A with trivial translation stabilizer, G_H° is simple modulo its centre; equivalently its nonzero derived Lie algebra is simple. This holds whether or not H is a translate of its inverse image under inversion.
hypotheses: n>2 is needed for the Albanese/Lefschetz step.
proofSteps: Assuming failure of simplicity, factor [m]_*Λ_H as two effective clean cycles of degree >1. Trivial stabilizer makes [m]|H generically injective, hence the left side remains reduced and irreducible.

Use the rational maps from the support factorization, extend them to maps from H to A, and factor them through Alb(H)=A by weak Lefschetz (dim H≥2). The addition identity becomes an identity of homomorphisms plus translation.

Write g₁:A→B₁ for the induced surjective homomorphism and Z₁ for the image of H. If Z₁=B₁ its Gauss degree is zero. Otherwise H is an irreducible component of g₁⁻¹Z₁ by dimension. The connected kernel preserves every such component; a positive-dimensional kernel would preserve the ample divisor, which is impossible. Thus g₁ is an isogeny onto A. Trivial stabilizer makes its restriction H→Z₁ generically one-to-one: outside the intersections with finitely many distinct kernel translates there are no collisions. Isogeny pushforward of conormals therefore preserves the Gauss degree N, forcing the other clean factor to have degree 1. There is no need to infer that g₁ is an isomorphism, a stronger step not justified by the printed full-preimage assertion.

nodes.statement: For n>2 under the preceding hypotheses, the image G_H* in GL_N is either a standard classical group SL_N, Sp_N or SO_N, an image of a spin or half-spin representation, or the image of ∧^k of the standard SL_m representation with 1<k<m−1. The exceptional minuscule images of E₆ and E₇ have dimensions 27 and 56 and are excluded because 6 divides N=n!d. Spin dimensions are powers of 2, so the same divisibility excludes them. The ∧²SL₄ image is SO₆ and belongs to the classical case.
hypotheses: Classify faithful images up to central isogeny; do not identify the image with SL_m when its exterior-power kernel is nontrivial.
proofSteps: Use the complete requested minuscule table, including types A–D and E₆,E₇ and the nonexistence in the remaining exceptional types.
Apply Weyl dimensions or the spin supplier. For n≥3, divisibility by 6 rules out powers of 2, 27 and 56. Keep the standard representations and interior exterior powers.

nodes.title: Inversion symmetry and the classical form
nodes.statement: When G_H* acts by a standard classical representation and N≥6, if H is not a translate of [−1]H, the image is SL_N. If H is such a translate, the resulting pairing on V_H is alternating for even n and symmetric for odd n, so the image is Sp_N or SO_N respectively. The pairing may be valued in a one-dimensional object; translating H to make it symmetric trivializes the geometric tensor factor. The connected derived image remains the stated group.
hypotheses: Smooth ample H, trivial stabilizer and n>2; conclusions are up to change of basis of V_H.
proofSteps: A self-duality of the irreducible derived representation gives a one-dimensional tensor factor in the geometric generated category. Identify it with a skyscraper and compare supports to obtain inversion up to translation.

For the inverse implication translate by a half-point over the algebraic closure. Use Verdier/Poincaré duality and the shift n−1 to compute the symmetry as (−1)^(n−1). Connected derived subgroups kill the line-valued similitude character.

sources.match: The parity is that of the support dimension n−1. The normal subgroup theorem concerns isometry groups, while arithmetic monodromy can lie in their similitude normalizers.

acceptance: Even ambient dimension gives an alternating form and even N.

Equivalently, for the finitely supported histogram h(j)=#{i:w_i=j}, this number is Σ_u Π_j binom(h(j),u(j)), over finitely supported u with 0≤u≤h, Σ_j u(j)=k and Σ_j j u(j)=t. Binomial coefficients use Nat.choose, including binom(a,a)=1; invalid occupancies contribute zero. This counts subsets, not ordered tuples.

proofSteps: Filter the actual finite set of k-subsets by its integer sum. Group subsets by their histogram to obtain the product of binomial coefficients.
For complements use the total weight T=Σ_iw_i. Translate all weights by b to add kb to every k-subset sum.

nodes.title: Hodge constraint on exterior powers
nodes.statement: If G_H* is the image of SL_m acting on ∧^k of its standard representation, with 1<k<m−1, then there exist integer weights w:Fin(m)→Z and s∈Z such that W(w,k,s+q)=dA(n,q) for every q∈Z. The Eulerian row is zero outside 0≤q<n. Complementing k-subsets and using Eulerian symmetry permits the normalization 2k≤m. Finite support and positive d are part of the assertion.
hypotheses: Smooth ample H of dimension n−1 over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field; trivial translation stabilizer; use compatible complex and p-adic realizations.
proofSteps: Choose a finite-order good character and a finitely generated field of definition. Spread the finite normalizer tensor constraints and specialize to a number-field point, retaining the inclusion of the arithmetic image in the exterior-power normalizer.

Use the requested Hodge–Tate cocharacter in the Zariski closure of the Galois image. Compare its graded fibre functor with the ordinary fibre functor over C_p; this comparison is required and is not a canonical equality of fibres.

The connected cocharacter lands in the connected exterior-power normalizer. After pulling it back by t↦t^k, lift to GL_m. The lifted standard weights are congruent modulo k because their differences are adjoint weights. Remove their common fractional part into an integral central shift s. nodes.title: Extremal occupancies and weight width
nodes.statement: Assume n≥2,d≥1,1<k<m−1,2k≤m and W(w,k,s+q)=dA(n,q) for every integral q. Let h be the finite weight histogram and u_min,u_max the unique histograms of minimum- and maximum-weight k-subsets (the subsets themselves need not be unique). Let v be the greatest occupied weight of u_min and v′ the least of u_max. Then v≤v′, u_min fills all h below v and none above, u_max fills all h above v′ and none below, and Σ_{i<v}(v−i)h(i)+Σ_{i>v′}(i−v′)h(i)+k(v′−v)=n−1. Every summand is nonnegative.

nodes.title: Classical convolution monodromy
nodes.statement: Let A/C have dimension n>2, and H⊂A be smooth ample with trivial translation stabilizer. Write d=[H]^n/n! and N=n!d. Then G_H contains as a normal subgroup SL_N when H is not a translate of [−1]H; if it is such a translate, the normal subgroup is Sp_N for even n and SO_N for odd n. nodes.title: Rigidity of constant tensor constituents
nodes.statement: Let X/C be smooth connected, A/C an abelian variety, and Y⊂X×A a smooth proper family of ample hypersurfaces. On A_η̄ let K=i_*F[n−1], G=G(K), G*=(G°)^der. Assume the geometric generic hypersurface has trivial translation stabilizer, G* is noncommutative connected simple with irreducible distinguished representation, and the family is not generically a translate of a fixed hypersurface by a section of A (equivalently here after spreading the unique translation). If a simple object in ⟨K⟩⊗ has a representative pulled back from A_C, then G* acts trivially on it.
hypotheses: Simple means simple modulo negligible objects, with a nonnegligible simple representative.
proofSteps: Compare two independent geometric generic fibres over X². Goursat gives either independent simple derived factors or a graph relation modulo scalars.

In the independent case a constant constituent is pulled back in both ways, so both simple factors act trivially. In the graph case use enough independent points of X^r to kill the finite outer-automorphism ambiguity.

The remaining scalar relation gives a one-dimensional factor between the two distinguished objects. Identify it with a skyscraper, hence translation. Trivial stabilizer makes the translating section unique and allows descent, contradicting the nonconstant hypothesis.

nodes.title: Independent coordinate convolution factors

Iterating, the axis-supported sum of c copies of K has group G^c. Under constant-part-rigidity, (G*)^c acts trivially on every constant tensor constituent of this axis-supported sum on A^c_η̄.
hypotheses: c≥1; all good characters and fibre comparisons are chosen compatibly.
proofSteps: A common quotient of the two generated groups would give isomorphic objects supported on the two different axes. Their common support is the origin, so the common quotient is trivial.

Apply induction on c. For a constant constituent nontrivial on a coordinate G*, twist generically and push to that coordinate. Proper base change preserves constancy, contradicting constant-part-rigidity. The required exact tensor pushforward restriction is included in the EDC.6 request.

Künneth/Leray, the projection formula and generic vanishing then give nonzero pH⁰(Rπ_*K′). The fibre-dimension bound provides its natural map to Rπ_*K′. Adjunction yields a constant perverse constituent of K, a contradiction.

nodes.title: Finite representations detecting a simple product
nodes.statement: Let G* be a noncommutative connected simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field acting faithfully and irreducibly on V, and let N=N_GL(V)(G*). Choose a Jordan bound J for subgroups of N finite modulo scalars and an N-representation W of dimension >J restricting irreducibly to G*. nodes.title: Prime-to-p Frobenius avoidance
nodes.statement: Let A/K be an abelian variety over a number field with good reduction at a place of residue characteristic p, fix lifts of its Frobenius in the two actions on finite-order character pairs, and choose m>0 whose Frobenius power fixes the Galois closure of K. Given c≥1 and a finite union S of torsion cosets in Π(A)^c, there is a finite union S′ of torsion cosets in Π(A) such that for each finite-order χ of order prime to p outside S′, some e₁,…,e_c∈Z give (Frob_p^(me₁)χ,…,Frob_p^(me_c)χ) outside S. The two actions are geometric transport and cyclotomic transport of character values.
hypotheses: Only prime-to-p torsion characters are asserted here. Fix a common algebraic closure and compatible embeddings for the transport.
proofSteps: Let M be the number of cosets in S. The case M=0 is immediate. Replace m by a multiple so the geometric restriction kernels and translating torsion data are stable under σ=Frob^m. On every prime-to-p Tate module the combined geometric/cyclotomic action has Weil eigenvalues of nonzero weight, so no positive power has eigenvalue 1.

For a fixed proper coset τT in Π(A)^c, choose a coordinate axis whose inverse image T_r is proper. Write T_r as the restriction kernel for a positive-dimensional B⊂A. For every 0≤e<e′≤M, equality of σ^eχ and σ^e′χ on B forces χ|B into a finite torsion set: the relevant σ^(e′−e)−1 has nonzero determinant. Taking inverse images under restriction gives a finite union of torsion translates of T_r. Collect these collision loci for all cosets and exponent pairs into S′.

For χ outside S′, fix all exponents other than e_r in {0,…,M}. At most one e_r can place the tuple in τT; two choices would give an excluded collision on B. Thus at most (M+1)^(c−1) tuples are bad for each coset and at most M(M+1)^(c−1)<(M+1)^c are bad in total. A good tuple exists. Exponents for the original Frobenius step are obtained by the integer scaling used when enlarging m.
The determinant argument here concerns prime-to-p torsion only. E6 records the omitted p-primary justification in the source, and E20 corrects the reversed word in its initial finite-box count.

nodes.title: Character generic in every conjugate
nodes.statement: For each embedding ι:K→Q̄ suppose S_ι is a finite union of torsion cosets in Π(A_ι). nodes.title: Period maps of isogeny pullbacks
nodes.statement: Fix a complex abelian variety A of dimension n≥2 and an ample line bundle L. Let M be the open subset of the complete linear system P(H⁰(A,L)) parameterizing smooth divisors, using the convention that points are nonzero sections modulo scalar. For m>0 let Y_m→M be the family [m]⁻¹H. The torsion-free integral middle cohomology with its polarization and Hodge filtration defines a period map Φ_m to the appropriate polarized period quotient. Its rational local system splits, after a coefficient extension, into character-isotypic summands H^(n−1)(H,Lχ), for characters of A[m]. The fixed class is in Pic(A), not merely NS(A).
hypotheses: Use polarizations from the fixed ample geometric data and finite level/markings when a period domain rather than its quotient is used.
proofSteps: Form the smooth-divisor open of the projective section space. Multiplication by m is finite étale in characteristic zero, so the pulled-back universal divisor is smooth proper.

Import the polarized integral variation and its period map, keeping the lattice modulo torsion. Decompose the finite abelian deck group after scalar extension; trace and pullback maps compare the variations for m|m′.

sources.match: Fixing an ample Picard class makes translations preserving it finite, which is indispensable to the period argument.

acceptance: For m=1 this is the usual middle-cohomology period map of smooth divisors in |L|.
The number of translates of one divisor retaining the same L is finite.
Fixing only a Néron–Severi class allows a positive-dimensional translation orbit and is not this parameter space.

nodes.title: Surface period finiteness by Torelli
nodes.statement: When dim A=2, the period map Φ₁ of smooth curves in the fixed complete linear system |L| has finite fibres. Here the polarization on H¹ is the canonical cup-product principal polarization. The genus is g=1+d≥2. No convolution simplicity assertion in dimension two is required.
hypotheses: A is a complex abelian surface, L is ample, and the parameter space is the smooth-divisor open M⊂|L|; the statement is vacuous when M is empty.
proofSteps: Use adjunction and the SC.3 Euler calculation to obtain g=1+d. A polarized integral weight-one Hodge structure determines the principally polarized Jacobian. The full-level Torelli theorem gives finite geometric fibres from the moduli of genus-g curves to the moduli of their polarized Jacobians.

Show that M→M_g has zero-dimensional geometric fibres. On a reduced connected component of such a fibre, the universal curve becomes a fixed curve C after the finite étale isomorphism cover; finite automorphisms for g≥2 and a fine level N≥3 justify this reduction. Fix c₀∈C. The pointed map C→A uniquely factors through J(C) by Abel–Jacobi, and the relative Hom space is unramified, so its homomorphism component is constant on a connected reduced parameter space.

Consequently the embedded images in A on that component differ only by translations. Translating a fixed divisor H₀ preserves O_A(H₀)≅L only for points in ker φ_L. Amplitude makes this kernel finite; hence the component has constant image in M. The fibre of M→M_g is a zero-dimensional finite-type algebraic space, so has finitely many geometric points.

Combine these finite fibres with Torelli and the weight-one comparison. Passing to and forgetting a finite level cover preserves fibre finiteness. This gives m=1 for n=2 and repairs the dimension mismatch in the source period proof.

sources.locator: Milne, Proposition 6.1, pp. 19–20, and Theorem 12.1, pp. 38–39; application to LS Proposition 4.11, pp. 37–38

nodes.title: Quasi-finite isogeny-pullback period map
nodes.statement: For the smooth-divisor space M of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety of dimension n≥2, some m>0 makes Φ_m quasi-finite, meaning every fibre is finite. For n=2 take m=1 by surface-period-finiteness. For n>2 the monodromy route passes to the finite generic translation-stabilizer quotient and retains the marked-period compatibility obligation G3. The general assertion is a target with that recorded proof obligation.
hypotheses: This is a target theorem with recorded proof gaps, not an implementation or a completed proof.
proofSteps: On M×M use the weight-zero Hom variation and the flat orbit of the diagonal identity tensor. CDK Corollary 1.3 makes its projected Hodge locus Z_m closed algebraic: multiply a rational tensor by a fixed denominator and use its fixed polarization norm to apply the finite bounded-norm theorem. A countable-union Hodge-locus statement alone would not suffice.

For m|m′ the trace-compatible identity condition gives Z_m′⊂Z_m. Along divisibility, Noetherianity gives a stabilized closed relation. A positive-dimensional period fibre then supplies an algebraic positive-dimensional family with constant period for every multiple of m. Integral polarizability makes its monodromy finite, and the deck-character decomposition makes every torsion-twist summand have finite monodromy.

Fixing L rules out constancy by translations. Quotient by the finite generic translation stabilizer, shrinking the family so that its action is fixed; the resulting ample family has trivial stabilizer. For n>2 apply simplicity and generic-big-monodromy to contradict finite monodromy for a torsion character outside the finite exceptional union.

For n=2 apply surface-period-finiteness instead. For n>2, G3 must certify that the chosen identity-orbit relations preserve every pullback/trace summand, are nested under divisibility and detect period fibres with the specified polarized marking conventions. Identity transport respects flat trace idempotents, but this must be reconciled with the quotient used for the period map.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.11, pp. 37–38; CDK, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.3, PDF p. 2
sources.match: The precise CDK finite theorem supplies the closedness interface. The surface case has a separate Torelli route; the higher-dimensional marked-period argument retains G3.

acceptance: Quasi-finite is fibre finiteness, not global injectivity or properness.
Only Picard-fixed parameter spaces are in scope.
The n=2 proof uses Torelli and rigid Hom spaces, with no appeal to the n>2 simplicity lemma.
